author: Stone-Zsela
assignment: Chief Justice Stone-Zsela assigns from the established judgment coalition. Before this assignment, the actual signed lead rows of prior effective Records were freshly recounted, using alphabetical case order for same-date events and including Records written earlier in this Run. Counts: Stone-Zsela 7; Stevens 8; O'Connor 8; Scalia 8; Kennedy 8; Souter 8; Thomas 7; Ginsburg 8; Breyer 9. Last counted event: NLRB v. Kentucky River Community Care, Inc. (2001-05-29). Eligible authors supporting every Court proposition: Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Kennedy, Souter, Ginsburg, Breyer. Balance pool (no more than one above the eligible minimum 7): Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Kennedy, Souter, Ginsburg. Selected author: Stone-Zsela. Fit and precise doctrinal formulation support self-assignment. Stone s approved position directly coordinates the recipient relationship, the separate necessity and reasonableness conditions, and both ways a modification can fundamentally alter competition. His formulation preserves actual trial findings while requiring essential features and individual competitive advantage to be examined separately, giving his authorship a concrete advantage in expressing the practical accommodation duty without a categorical sports exemption or automatic entitlement. Ginsburg is the strongest alternative through her individualized accommodation positions and can carry the rule, but Stone has the lower count and his case-specific organization best preserves the two distinct alteration inquiries. All seven already join; no expansion or new judicial choice is inferred. The selected final formulation preserves every frozen join; no reassignment or changed commitment is needed.
